:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
Find the derivative of $\mathbf f(t) + 2\mathbf g(t)$ with respect to $t,$ where $\mathbf f(t)$ and $\mathbf g(t)$ are defined as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =(4{t}^{2}+9)\,i-(\frac{1}{t-2})\,j+\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,k \\ g(t) & =(4t-1)\,i+{e}^{3t}\,j+\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,k\end{aligned}
$$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
Using the constant multiple rule and the sum rule, we have

$$
(\mathbf f(t) + 2\mathbf g(t))' = \mathbf f'(t) + 2\mathbf g'(t).
$$

Now, let's find the derivative of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4{t}^{2}+9)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\frac{1}{t-2})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)\,k \\  & =8t\,i+\frac{1}{(t-2)^{2}}\,j-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,k, \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t-1)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{3t})j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)k \\  & =4\,i+3{e}^{3t}\,j-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(f(t)+2g(t))^{′} & ={f}^{′}(t)+2{g}^{′}(t) \\  & =(8t\,i+\frac{1}{(t-2)^{2}}\,j-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,k)+2(4\,i+3{e}^{3t}\,j-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,k) \\  & =8(t+1)\,i+(\frac{1}{(t-2)^{2}}+6{e}^{3t})\,j-6\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem: Find $\big( u(t) \mathbf g(t) \big)'$ where ![](images/9e/9e23d542bfc56d506f5437a35a92c304d618109ef60086e1f5a7a4fee57d8a80.png) and $u(t) = t.$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
Using the scalar function multiple rule, we have

$$
\big( u(t) \mathbf g(t) \big)' = u'(t) \mathbf{g}(t) + u(t) \mathbf{g}'(t).
$$

Let's find $\mathbf g'(t)$ and $u'(t),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-t) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{t} \\ -1 \\ 2{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}] \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)=1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(u(t)g(t))^{′} & ={u}^{′}(t)g(t)+u(t){g}^{′}(t) \\  & =1\cdot [\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡t \\ -t \\ {e}^{2t}\end{aligned}]+t\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{t} \\ -1 \\ 2{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡t \\ -t \\ {e}^{2t}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -t \\ 2t{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1+\operatorname{ln}⁡t \\ -2t \\ (2t+1){e}^{2t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem: Find $(\mathbf f \circ u)'(t),$ if $\mathbf f(u) = \ln u \, \mathbf i + (u^2+5) \, \mathbf j + 4u \, \mathbf k$ and $u(t) =2t^3.$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
By the chain rule, we have 

$$
(\mathbf f \circ u)'(t) = \mathbf{f}'(u(t)) u'(t).
$$

Now, let's find the derivative of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(u) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}(\operatorname{ln}⁡u)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}({u}^{2}+5)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}(4u)k \\  & =\frac{1}{u}\,i+2u\,j+4\,k, \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{3})=6{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(f∘u)^{′}(t) & ={f}^{′}(u(t)){u}^{′}(t) \\  & =(\frac{1}{u(t)}\,i+2u(t)\,j+4\,k){u}^{′}(t) \\  & =(\frac{1}{2{t}^{3}}\,i+2(2{t}^{3})\,j+4\,k)\cdot 6{t}^{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{t}\,i+24{t}^{5}\,j+24{t}^{2}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
Find $\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt} (\mathbf f \cdot \mathbf g)(t),$ given the following functions $\mathbf f(t)$ and $\mathbf g(t)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =\sqrt{t}\,i+{t}^{2}j \\ g(t) & =\frac{1}{t}i+{e}^{t}j\end{aligned}
$$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
Using the dot product rule, we have

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(\mathbf{f} \cdot \mathbf{g})(t) = \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(\mathbf{f}(t)) \cdot \mathbf{g}(t) + \mathbf{f}(t) \cdot \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(\mathbf{g}(t))
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}f(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{t})i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})j \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}\,i+2t\,j, \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}g(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t})i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t})j \\  & =-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}\,i+{e}^{t}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\eqalign{
\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt} (\mathbf f \cdot \mathbf g)(t)
&= \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(\mathbf{f}(t)) \cdot \mathbf{g}(t) + \mathbf{f}(t) \cdot \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(\mathbf{g}(t)) \[3pt]
&= \left(\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{t}} \,\mathbf i +2t \, \mathbf j \right) \cdot \left(\dfrac{1}{t} \,  \mathbf i + e^t \,  \mathbf j \right) +
\left(\sqrt{t} \,  \mathbf i + t^2 \,  \mathbf j \right) \cdot \left(-\dfrac{1}{t^2}  \, \mathbf i + e^t \, \mathbf j  \right) \[3pt]		 
&=\dfrac{1}{2t\sqrt{t}}  +2te^t    +  \left(-\dfrac{\sqrt{t}}{t^2}\right)    + t^2e^t \[3pt]
&=\dfrac{\sqrt{t}}{2t^2}  -  \dfrac{\sqrt{t}}{t^2} +2te^t   + t^2e^t  \[3pt]
&= -\dfrac{\sqrt{t}}{2t^2} +\left(2t+t^2\right)e^t.
}
$$
